findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The shipped review prompt assures reviewers that every named test exists in the branch, but Close publishes unmatched names without checking that their files exist. The new command test names `__tests__/greeting.js` without creating that file and asserts that Close publishes it as `not checked` (`tests/test_close_checks_named_tests.py:21-23, 51-53, 114`). The worker brief and shipped skill also say the list contains only tests Close ran, contradicting the recorded allowance for `not run` and `not checked` entries. This is distinct from the accepted finding about a worker-authored heading: these are false claims in Forge's own guidance.
findings.title: Not done: Review guidance falsely says every named test exists in the branch

stop.reason: Coordinator (all Harm 2, reversible; round 12, and round 9 was announced as the last): accept and merge; one follow-up fix right after covers all four: close writes its own 'Proof list:' heading, a mixed-language line marks each unmatched name, inherited pytest methods match their run result, and results are recorded relative to the repo root so sibling packages stay apart.

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
